subject.title: [Bug]: 2 codex accounts, same machine, same docs, one has balloon startup cost

question: Should default local Codex stdio app-server state move from per-agent CODEX_HOME to per-auth-profile CODEX_HOME for OpenClaw-managed auth profiles, and if so what upgrade/reset behavior should existing users get?
rationale: The source-backed bug path is clear, but the fix changes persisted native Codex state ownership and can affect existing users' auth, sessions, plugin data, and diagnostics.

options.title: Define account-scoped isolation first
options.body: Use per-auth-profile Codex homes for managed auth profiles, but require a documented migration/reset/cleanup plan and live two-account proof before implementation lands.

options.title: Keep per-agent state and solve elsewhere
options.body: Preserve the current storage boundary and instead investigate a narrower Codex cache/session reset or context-ledger fix if account state sharing is considered intentional.

options.title: Defer until live repro
options.body: Keep this issue open while collecting a redacted current-main two-account run before choosing a storage behavior change.

recommendation.title: Define account-scoped isolation first
recommendation.body: Use per-auth-profile Codex homes for managed auth profiles, but require a documented migration/reset/cleanup plan and live two-account proof before implementation lands.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged the central OAuth work and recently changed Codex homeScope/thread-sharing behavior, making them the strongest available owner for the state-boundary decision.
